comment.body: PRE-DISPATCH STEER (overseer, arm-time — fold into your first brief). Semantic traps your grep gate cannot catch; all are hard requirements: (1) NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME must be COMPUTED from `ip -br addr` — only rails that actually carry a routable IP. Rail 1 (thunderbolt1) is trained but IP-UNCONFIGURED (169.254.x link-local, no peer): hardcoding both rails passes the grep and hangs RCCL bootstrap. In practice only thunderbolt0 (10.99.0.x /30) qualifies. (2) NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 UNCONDITIONALLY in host/fn-env.sh — not conditional on device detection. ibverbs devices exist on BOTH nodes by design (usb4_rdma0 + usb4_rdma5); without the pin RCCL autodetects verbs and silently rides the unproven RDMA path. Sockets are the transport of record this run. (3) NEVER export a probe-read engine default: VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM, VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM, VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER* are read via is_set() probes — exporting the default diverts the oracle into a hard raise (spec F.9). (4) Receipts must match scripts/receipts-verify.py EXACTLY — run it against your own output before declaring done. (5) Worker-side actions ride the ethernet wire (10.99.9.2), never a 10.99.0.x Thunderbolt rail — rails carry tensors only. (6) cluster-up is reap-then-gate: reap stale processes first, then gate on health, in that order.

comment.body: PRE-DISPATCH STEER (overseer, community intel — flashnext#4, no scope change). Multi-sequence QSA gather on gfx1151 HIP has documented wrong-output/crash behavior in the llama.cpp stack. Our vLLM code path differs, but harden the matrix against it: (1) the bench matrix MUST record the concurrency (number of in-flight sequences) per arm in its output rows; (2) if any token fingerprint diverges across runs of the same arm, the harness must byte-compare a serial (concurrency=1) replay of that arm before its numbers are trusted — flag the arm as suspect in the output rather than averaging over the divergence. Fingerprint divergence at concurrency>1 with a clean serial replay is the QSA-gather signature; record it, do not paper over it.

comment.body: OVERSEER DIAGNOSIS (from your serve3 log, applies to current/future attempts): the engine dies in determine_available_memory with HIP OOM allocating EXACTLY 274877906944 bytes = 256 GiB = 2x total device memory (free 120.7 GiB, total 128 GiB). A 2x-total allocation in the KV-cache sizing probe is the unified-memory/GTT double-count signature on this APU: the fork carries a GTT-routed MemorySnapshot.measure specifically for this hardware, with kill-switch VLLM_ROCM_APU_UNIFIED_MEMORY=0. Set VLLM_ROCM_APU_UNIFIED_MEMORY=0 in the serve env for the proxy first light (VRAM-only accounting is correct for the small proxy checkpoint) and retry; if that clears it, record the env choice in your receipt data and in the script so cp-proxy reproduces it. Do NOT chase this by shrinking gpu_memory_utilization — 0.6 of 128 GiB can never legitimately request 256 GiB; the measure is double-counting, the utilization knob is not the bug.
